observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. South: a wide, domed oval shell crusted with pale green lichen rosettes. A small head pokes out at the front centre with two glossy black eyes. The head is lowered onto a little scatter of lichen crumbs, and about six to eight short jointed legs splay out on each side. East: a side profile of the same domed, lichen-spotted shell. The head is at the right with a black eye and short segmented antennae, the mouth is down in a small crumb patch, and segmented legs show underneath. North: the shell seen from behind and from noticeably higher up. Its dorsal surface fills the view, and it narrows to a rounded point at the bottom like a tail end. Two antennae and a sliver of head show beyond the far rim, legs radiate around the edge, and there is no face. North is clearly taller on the canvas than the other two.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution. A low, wide, dome-shelled arthropod shown face-on. The head is tucked under the shell's front rim, with two round black eyes and a broad, blunt muzzle pressed onto a small patch of lichen debris. Shell plates have a centre seam and are speckled with lichen. Brown jointed legs sit along both sides. Painterly, realistic texture, with a thin dark outline.
observed.east.png: Side profile. The shell is a long, low-to-medium dome with a segmented rim. The head and neck point down and right, the mouth sits in a scatter of lichen flakes and crumbs, and there are short knobbed antennae and a single black eye. Legs are tucked beneath. It reads as an isopod or tortoise-like bug.
observed.north.png: Rear view from a steeper angle. Almost the whole dorsal shell is visible as a rounded shield that tapers to a blunt point toward the viewer. The far rim shows a head bump with two antennae. Legs splay out radially on all sides, more like an overhead view than the low game camera. No eyes.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the crustweevil is a tiny flat brown smudge beside the vanilla human, much smaller than a hand. At 32 px per cell it is a speck smaller than the rat, barely visible as a grey-brown dot.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head face-on, with two eyes and a muzzle toward the camera, under the shell's front rim.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the shell tapering to a rear point. Only antennae show beyond the far rim; there are no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: North is drawn from a much higher angle than south and east. The full dorsal shield and legs radiating on all sides read close to top-down.

SIGNATURE.seen: A small crust grazer with its mouth down in lichen: the lichen-crusted shell and the grazing head lowered onto lichen crumbs are legible in south and east.

ALIEN.seen: Reads as a woodlouse or tortoise-like bug, but the lichen-overgrown shell, splayed many-legged stance and grazing head keep it from being a clean Earth species. Most departures are present.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 (tiny, at centimetre scale, on the crust): present. It is tiny in the scale panel and grazes crumbs on the ground. 2 (broad, low grazing mouth held down): present. STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic, with texture on the shell and legs and a thin dark outline. The round glossy black eyes are slightly endearing but not cartoonish.

OURS.seen: Original art. It does not match any vanilla or known mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha. The only ground element is a small scatter of lichen crumbs under the mouth, which the card's departure 4 asks for. There is no backdrop or shadow.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale, each about the same height. South and north are a symmetric triangle of about 40 grey, wingless, flattened bugs with eight legs, like ticks or mites. They are stacked tightly from a wide base up to one bug at the apex, so the group reads as a heap or pyramid. East is a diagonal stream of the same grey bugs in side profile, rising from a dense low cluster at bottom-left to scattered single bugs at top-right, with legs trailing and short antennae forward. There is no ground, shadow or backdrop.
observed.south.png: Full-res south: a triangular pile of grey, wingless, tick- or mite-like bugs. Most show a small head and forelegs toward the camera at the bottom of a rounded, flat carapace. They are bigger at the base and smaller toward the top. The rendering is soft and painterly-realistic, with a subtle dark edge. The alpha is clean.
observed.east.png: Full-res east: the same bugs in side profile, all heading right and up in a diagonal column from the lower-left to the upper-right. The lower ones are clustered and the upper ones are spaced out and appear airborne, with legs dangling. Short thin antennae point forward. The colour is uniform ash-grey and the alpha is clean.
observed.north.png: Full-res north: a triangular pile like the south one. The bugs show the domed rear of the carapace, with small head knobs and short antennae at the top edge of each body pointing away. No eyes are visible. They are all grey, with clean alpha.
